title: AI photo-to-recipe import (core feature)
description: The core reason this app exists: let Pete snap/upload one or more photos of a recipe (a cookbook page, a handwritten card, a series of screenshots from a Pinterest pin or a blog post) and have Claude read them and turn them into a clean, structured, ad-free recipe - title, ingredients, steps, timing/servings if visible - ready to review and save. This replaces screenshotting/bookmarking recipes on ad-laden sites like Pinterest just to reference them later.
design: New page (e.g. import.html) - user selects 1+ images, they upload to a private storage path (new bucket 'recipe-imports' or a subpath of existing 'recipe-photos', {user_id}/... gated same as migration 002), then a Supabase Edge Function sends the image(s) to Claude (vision) with a tool-schema prompt asking for {title, description, prep_minutes, cook_minutes, servings, ingredients: [{quantity,unit,name}], instructions: [string], source_name, source_url} matching the recipes table shape exactly, so the result can prefill add-recipe.html's form fields directly for review/edit before saving (never auto-saved - user always confirms). Mirrors Houstory's upload.html -> analyze-media edge function pattern (houstory-96t.2/.3), but returns the recipes schema instead of a freeform description. Multi-image input matters - a single recipe is often 2-4 screenshots stitched together (intro, ingredients, steps).
acceptance_criteria: Can select 2-3 photos of a real recipe (e.g. a Pinterest screenshot series), submit, and get back a structured draft with correct title/ingredients/steps that prefills the add-recipe form for review before saving. Handles a single photo too. Original source photos are stored and remain viewable/attached to the saved recipe.
close_reason: Built and verified end-to-end: import.html uploads photo(s) to recipe-photos/{user_id}/imports/, calls the new extract-recipe edge function (Claude Sonnet 5, forced tool_choice to extract_recipe matching the recipes table shape), result prefills add-recipe.html for review before saving, source photos persist via recipes.source_photo_paths (migration 004) and render on recipe.html. Tested with a synthetic cluttered recipe screenshot (ads/nav/comments included) - Claude correctly extracted only the real recipe content and ignored the clutter. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret configured on the Supabase project; function deployed.

title: Recipes v2: AI photo import, Google sign-in, finished-dish photos, richer search
description: Next phase after the v1 core loop (recipes-62x, closed). Pete's stated goal: capture recipes from diverse places (screenshots, photo of a cookbook page, Pinterest pins) so nothing gets lost, without living in an ad-laden site like Pinterest to reference them later. Four workstreams, each filed as its own child issue: Google sign-in, AI-powered photo-to-recipe import (the core differentiator), finished-dish photos, and better search/categories.

title: Recipes v1: personal recipe box core loop
description: Ship the core loop: sign up/sign in, add a recipe (title/ingredients/steps/tags/timing), browse/search/filter your recipe list, view a recipe, edit/delete it. Scaffolded 2026-08-21 mirroring the Five Wonders/Houstory infra pattern (static HTML/CSS/JS, Supabase Postgres+Storage, GitHub Pages, bd).
acceptance_criteria: Can sign up, add a recipe with ingredients+steps+tags, see it in the list, filter by tag, search by title, view detail, edit it, and delete it - all working against the live Supabase project.
close_reason: v1 core loop shipped and verified end-to-end in browser (2026-08-21). Superseded by the v2 epic (recipes-022) for the next phase of work.

title: Redesign homepage: Google sign-in on landing, rebrand to Morse Recipes, remove separate login page
description:
Rework index.html into the single entry point for the app, replacing the current marketing-page-plus-separate-login.html flow. Four asks from Pete (2026-08-25):

1. Add the 'Sign in with Google' button directly to index.html (currently only on login.html).
2. Rename the app from 'Recipes' to 'Morse Recipes' - the page <title> and header on index.html at minimum; likely wants this applied consistently across all pages (app.html, add-recipe.html, recipe.html, profile.html, import.html, and the removed login.html's replacement) so tab titles and headers don't clash - confirm scope before implementing broadly.
3. Change the tagline/description text on index.html from the current 'Your personal recipe box.' to something about sharing the Morse family's favorite recipes.
4. Remove login.html entirely. Signed-out visitors see the marketing copy + Google sign-in (and open question: does email+password sign-in move onto index.html too, or does Google become the only sign-in method? Pete didn't say to drop email+password, but 'remove the sign in page' + 'adds Google sign-in to the homepage' reads like Google becomes primary/only - confirm before dropping email+password entirely, some users may still want it as a fallback). Signed-in visitors see 'Welcome, <name>!' (from profiles.first_name via the existing ensureProfile() logic, falling back to email if no name set) with a sign-out option.
design: Open question to confirm with Pete before/during implementation: does the signed-in 'Welcome, <name>!' state on index.html also need a way into the actual recipe list (link to app.html), or does index.html effectively become app.html (i.e. do the two merge)? Defaulting to: welcome message + sign out + a link into 'Your recipes' (app.html), keeping app.html as the actual recipe list/search page, unless told otherwise. Google sign-in wiring (signInWithOAuth, ensureProfile()) already exists and works (recipes-022.1, closed) - this issue is about moving/adding that UI to index.html and building the signed-in-state view, not building OAuth from scratch. Every other page currently redirects unauthenticated users to login.html (requireSession() pattern) - if login.html is removed, requireSession()'s redirect target needs to change to index.html (or wherever the sign-in UI lives) across add-recipe.html, recipe.html, profile.html, import.html, app.html.
acceptance_criteria: Visiting the site signed out shows 'Morse Recipes' branding, the new family-sharing description, and a working Google sign-in button - no separate /login.html page exists (or it redirects to index.html). Visiting while signed in shows 'Welcome, <name>!' with a sign-out control. All other pages' auth redirects still work correctly with login.html gone.
close_reason: Built and verified end-to-end (2026-08-25). Went with the defaults noted on the issue: 'Morse Recipes' branding applied site-wide (all page titles/headers), Google becomes the only sign-in method (email+password dropped along with login.html), and the signed-in homepage keeps a link into 'Your recipes' (app.html) alongside the welcome message and sign-out. login.html deleted; every page's requireSession() now redirects to index.html instead. index.html gained its own ensureProfile() (same logic as app.html) since it's now the OAuth landing target and needs first_name immediately for the welcome message. Verified: signed-out homepage shows new branding/tagline/Google button; signed-in shows 'Welcome, Peter!' (pulled correctly from Google metadata, backfilled into profiles.first_name/avatar_url); all 5 other pages (app/add-recipe/recipe/profile/import) redirect unauthenticated visits to index.html with no 404s; authenticated pages still work normally.

title: Better search: by ingredient, and category vs. tag
description: Current search (app.html) only matches recipe title, client-side, against whatever's already loaded. Tag filter chips exist and work but are the only 'category' concept today. Pete asked for 'a way to search recipes and categories' - need to decide whether categories are a new distinct concept (a single required grouping per recipe, e.g. cuisine or meal type) layered on top of the existing free-form multi-tag system, or whether tags already cover it and search just needs to get better (e.g. matching ingredients, not just title).
design: At minimum: extend app.html's search to also match against ingredient names (currently only recipes.title, loaded client-side - ingredients are already fetched-able from the JSONB column, or could use a Postgres full-text/GIN index for server-side search once the recipe count grows past what's comfortable to filter client-side). Open question for Pete before building: does 'categories' mean introduce a distinct single-select category field (e.g. Breakfast/Dinner/Dessert) separate from the existing multi-tag system, or is tagging already the intended category mechanism and this is just about search quality? Confirm before implementing the schema change.
acceptance_criteria: Typing an ingredient name (not just a title word) into search surfaces matching recipes. Categories/tags are filterable and it's clear from the UI which concept (tags vs. a new category field) is in play.

title: Finished-dish photos on a recipe
description: Let the user attach photo(s) of how the finished dish actually turned out, separate from the source recipe photos captured during AI import. Distinguishes 'photo of the source I extracted this from' (import feature) from 'photo of what I made'.
design: recipes.photo_path column already exists (migration 001) but is unused - decide whether it's enough for a single hero photo, or whether finished-dish photos should be their own list (multiple attempts over time, e.g. cook it twice, both turn out differently) similar to a lightweight media table. The recipe-photos storage bucket and its {user_id}/... RLS policies already exist (migration 002) and are ready to receive uploads - only the UI (upload control on add-recipe.html or recipe.html, plus rendering on recipe.html) is missing.
acceptance_criteria: From a recipe's detail or edit page, can upload a photo of the finished dish and see it displayed on the recipe detail view.

title: Google sign-in for Recipes
description: Add Google OAuth sign-in alongside the existing email+password flow, mirroring Houstory's login.html (houstory-96t.11) and Five Wonders' pattern. Currently login.html/add-recipe flow is email+password only, requiring Admin-API confirmation for new signups since email confirmation is on by default.
design: Mirror Houstory: sb.auth.signInWithOAuth({provider:'google', options:{redirectTo: origin+'/app.html'}}). Requires enabling the Google provider in the Supabase dashboard (Auth > Providers) for project hhkxmuxcmjzvpjvctgqk and configuring OAuth consent/client in Google Cloud Console - this is a manual dashboard step, not just code. On first Google sign-in, ensureProfile() should seed profiles.first_name/last_name/avatar_url from user_metadata (given_name/family_name/picture), same as Houstory's app.html ensureProfile().
acceptance_criteria: Sign-in page shows a 'Sign in with Google' button; clicking it completes OAuth and lands on app.html with a session; profiles row is created/backfilled from Google metadata; existing email+password sign-in still works unchanged.
notes: Decision 2026-08-25: separate/new Google OAuth client for Recipes, not reusing Houstory's. Code is done and pushed (login.html Google button + signInWithOAuth, app.html ensureProfile()). Blocked on Pete completing two manual steps outside CLI/agent reach: (1) create the OAuth client in Google Cloud Console with redirect URI https://hhkxmuxcmjzvpjvctgqk.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback, (2) enable the Google provider + paste client id/secret in the Supabase dashboard (Authentication > Providers) for project hhkxmuxcmjzvpjvctgqk. Once done, verify end-to-end in browser before closing.
close_reason: Verified 2026-08-25: Sign in with Google button correctly redirects to Google's real OAuth consent screen (accounts.google.com, 'continue to hhkxmuxcmjzvpjvctgqk.supabase.co', no client/config errors) after Pete configured the Google Cloud OAuth client, enabled the provider in Supabase, and fixed Site URL/Redirect URLs (was defaulting to localhost:3000, causing the post-login bounce to localhost). Could not complete the actual login myself (needs Pete's real Google credentials) - Pete to do one real sign-in to confirm the final landing on app.html works, but everything up to that point is confirmed working.
